Get started with inshape

Source: vignettes/inshape.Rmd
inshape.Rmd

Register microdata comes in a few shapes: one row per unit, one row per unit and period (a panel), or one row per spell with a start and an end. Every analysis assumes the shape is right, and the errors that break it are silent: a duplicated key multiplies rows in a join, a missing year looks like an exit, an overlapping spell gives a person two addresses at once.

inshape checks the shape before anything is built on it, in two steps. The describe_*() functions look at the structure and judge nothing; the ensure_*() functions are checkpoints: each states one rule, warns or aborts with the rows that break it, and returns the data, so it sits in a pipeline.

Function The rule Returns
describe_key() (look) duplicated keys, exact copies vs. conflicts a summary
describe_panel() (look) units, gaps, entries, exits, patterns a summary
describe_spells() (look) gaps, transfers, overlapping and nested spells a summary
describe_varying() (look) which columns vary within units a summary
describe_codes() (look) how the codes of a column change over periods a summary
describe_changes() (look) what changed between two extracts a summary
ensure_codes() a coded column holds only codes from the code list the data
ensure_constant() sex, birth date and the like are constant within a unit the data
ensure_unique() the key columns identify each row the data
ensure_balanced() every unit is observed in every period, or has no gaps the data
ensure_no_overlap() a unit’s spells do not overlap the data
ensure_within() no rows after death or emigration, or before birth the data
merge_spells() (conversion) spells recorded as several, merged merged spells
spells_to_panel() (conversion) spells to a period panel a panel
add_spell_status() (conversion) status from spells on an existing panel the data plus status

Look first: describe_panel() and describe_key()

A rule is easier to choose when you have seen the data. describe_panel() summarises a panel in one pass: how many units are observed throughout, who enters and leaves when, where the gaps are, and which participation patterns are common, as Stata’s xtdescribe does.

persons <- tibble(
  cpr  = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "d", "d", "d", "d"),
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2022, 2022, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2022)
)

describe_panel(persons, cpr, year)
#> ── Panel: cpr by year ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 10 rows, 4 units, 3 periods, 2020-2022
#> 
#> • Observed in every period: 2 units (50.0%)
#> • With gaps: 1 unit (25.0%), 1 missing unit-period inside their span
#> • Duplicated unit-periods: 1 (1 extra row)
#> 
#> By period:
#>     period units entries exits  gaps
#>   1   2020     3      NA     0     0
#>   2   2021     2       0     0     1
#>   3   2022     4       1    NA     0
#> 
#> Most common patterns:
#>     pattern units share
#>   1 111         2 50.0%
#>   2 1.1         1 25.0%
#>   3 ..1         1 25.0%

A period with no units, or a sudden fall in units, is the sign of a broken extract. The counts are there to use as well, e.g. describe_panel(persons, cpr, year)$by_period.

describe_key() looks at a key. When it is not unique, the question is what the duplicates are: exact copies, which can be dropped, or rows that disagree, which need a rule. It tells them apart and names the columns the copies disagree in:

firms <- tibble(
  cvr      = c("1", "1", "2", "2", "3"),
  year     = 2024,
  industry = c("A", "A", "B", "C", "A")
)

describe_key(firms, cvr, year)
#> ── Key: cvr, year ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 5 rows, 3 distinct keys
#> 
#> • Duplicated keys: 2 (4 rows, 2 extra rows)
#> • Exact copies, identical in every column: 1 of 2 keys
#> • Copies differ in: industry (1)
#> • Copies per duplicated key: 2 (2)

Keys: ensure_unique()

Duplicate keys are the most common error in register data, and the most costly one sits right before a join. A lookup table with a duplicated key makes left_join() multiply rows without a word. Check the key first:

df <- tibble(
  cvr  = c("11111111", "22222222", "11111111"),
  year = c(2024, 2024, 2024)
)

df |>
  ensure_unique(cvr, year, warn_msg = "Duplicate company-years")
#> Warning in ensure_unique(df, cvr, year, warn_msg = "Duplicate company-years"): Duplicate company-years
#> ℹ 2 rows in 1 group:
#>     dupid cvr       year
#>     <int> <chr>    <dbl>
#>   1     1 11111111  2024
#>   2     1 11111111  2024

The reported rows carry a dupid, so the copies in each group sit together.

Panels: ensure_balanced()

A yearly register extract is a panel: one row per person (or company) and year. Whether it is balanced, every unit present in every year, decides which methods are valid and often reveals a broken extract.

panel <- tibble(
  cpr  = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c"),
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2022, 2022)
)

ensure_balanced(panel, cpr, year)
#> Warning in ensure_balanced(panel, cpr, year): Panel is not balanced: missing cpr-year combinations
#> ℹ 3 rows found:
#>     cpr    year
#>     <chr> <dbl>
#>   1 b      2021
#>   2 c      2020
#>   3 c      2021

Real populations are rarely balanced. People are born, die and migrate. What usually should hold is that a unit, once present, does not skip a year before it leaves. gaps_only = TRUE checks that: c entering in 2022 is fine, b missing in 2021 is not.

ensure_balanced(panel, cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE)
#> Warning in ensure_balanced(panel, cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE): Gaps in panel: missing cpr-year combinations
#> ℹ 1 row found:
#>     cpr    year
#>     <chr> <dbl>
#>   1 b      2021

By default the expected years are those found in the data, so a year that was never loaded goes unnoticed. State the years you expect to catch that as well:

ensure_balanced(panel, cpr, year, periods = 2015:2024, gaps_only = TRUE)

Spells: ensure_no_overlap()

The other shape of register data is spells: address periods, employment, benefit periods. A person has only one address at a time, so overlapping spells within a person are an error:

addresses <- tibble(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  start = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-06-01")),
  end   = as.Date(c("2020-12-31", NA,           "2020-06-30", "2021-12-31"))
)

ensure_no_overlap(addresses, cpr, start, end)
#> Warning in ensure_no_overlap(addresses, cpr, start, end): Overlapping spells per cpr
#> ℹ 2 rows in 1 group:
#>     overlap_id cpr   start      end
#>          <int> <chr> <date>     <date>
#>   1          1 b     2020-01-01 2020-06-30
#>   2          1 b     2020-06-01 2021-12-31

Spells are closed intervals, and a missing end means the spell is ongoing. The reported rows carry an overlap_id that groups spells overlapping each other, the same idea as dupid.

Before requiring that, look at how the spells relate to each other. describe_spells() takes each unit’s spells in order and says, for each, how it relates to the earlier ones: after a gap, adjacent (starting the day after one ends, often a transfer recorded as two spells), touching on one shared day, overlapping, nested or a duplicate. In patient registers up to a quarter of the entries can be such transfers, and counting spells without merging them first inflates every count.

admissions <- tibble(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c"),
  start = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-11", "2020-03-01",
                    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-05", "2021-06-01")),
  end   = as.Date(c("2020-01-10", "2020-01-20", "2020-03-05",
                    "2020-01-31", "2020-01-10", NA))
)

describe_spells(admissions, cpr, start, end)
#> ── Spells: start to end per cpr ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 6 rows, 6 usable spells, 3 units
#> 
#> • Ongoing (no end): 1
#> • Units with overlapping spells: 1 (33.3%)
#> 
#> Relation to the unit's earlier spells:
#>     relation    spells
#>   1 gap              1
#>   2 adjacent         1
#>   3 touching         0
#>   4 overlapping      0
#>   5 nested           1
#>   6 duplicate        0
#> 
#> Gaps between spells, in days:
#>         n   min   q25 median  mean   q75   max
#>   1     1    40    40     40    40    40    40
#> 
#> Length of ended spells, in days:
#>         n   min   q25 median  mean   q75   max
#>   1     5     5     6     10  12.4    10    31

merge_spells() merges them: by default spells that overlap or follow the next day become one, from the first start to the latest end, and n_spells counts what was merged. max_gap = 30 also merges spells less than a month apart, a readmission counted as the same episode, and by merges only spells that agree in a column such as the employer:

merge_spells(admissions, cpr, start, end)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   cpr   start      end        n_spells
#>   <chr> <date>     <date>        <int>
#> 1 a     2020-01-01 2020-01-20        2
#> 2 a     2020-03-01 2020-03-05        1
#> 3 b     2020-01-01 2020-01-31        2
#> 4 c     2021-06-01 NA                1

Attributes of the unit: describe_varying() and ensure_constant()

Sex and birth date belong to the person, not to the year, yet a panel repeats them on every row, and a person with two values is an error, usually of linkage or of a correction applied to some years only. describe_varying() shows which columns vary within units, from the constant to the varying. A column that varies for a handful of units out of millions is rarely meant to vary:

persons <- tibble(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c"),
  year   = c(2020, 2021, 2020, 2021, 2020, 2021),
  sex    = c("F", "F", "M", "F", "M", NA),
  income = c(100, 120, 90, 95, 80, 85)
)

describe_varying(persons, cpr)
#> ── Within cpr ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 3 units, 3 columns
#> 
#>     column varying share   partly_missing all_missing
#>   1 sex          1 33.33%               1           0
#>   2 income       3 100.00%              0           0
#>   3 year         3 100.00%              0           0

ensure_constant() turns that into a rule and lists every row of the units that break it. A missing value is not a contradiction, so c passes:

ensure_constant(persons, cpr, sex)
#> Warning in ensure_constant(persons, cpr, sex): Varies within units: sex per cpr
#> ℹ 2 rows found:
#>     cpr   sex    year income
#>     <chr> <chr> <dbl>  <dbl>
#>   1 b     M      2020     90
#>   2 b     F      2021     95

Codes over time: describe_codes() and ensure_codes()

Code lists change: municipalities merge, industry codes are revised. describe_codes() shows when each code occurs, so a revision stands out as a period with many new and many gone codes, and a typo as a code seen once:

residents <- tibble(
  year = rep(2018:2021, each = 4),
  municipality = c("955", "956", "957", NA,    "955", "956", "957", "957",
                   "960", "956", "957", "95",  "960", "965", "957", "956")
)

describe_codes(residents, municipality, year)
#> ── Codes: municipality by year ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 16 rows, 6 codes, 4 periods, 2018-2021
#> 
#> • In every period: 2 codes (33.3%)
#> • Skipping periods: 0 codes (0.0%)
#> • Rows with a missing municipality: 1
#> 
#> By period:
#>     period codes   new  gone missing
#>   1   2018     3    NA    NA       1
#>   2   2019     3     0     0       0
#>   3   2020     4     2     1       0
#>   4   2021     4     1     1       0
#> 
#> Codes not in every period, skipping first:
#>     code  first  last periods  gaps  rows
#>   1 95     2020  2020       1     0     1
#>   2 965    2021  2021       1     0     1
#>   3 955    2018  2019       2     0     2
#>   4 960    2020  2021       2     0     2

ensure_codes() requires the codes of a code list:

ensure_codes(residents, municipality, c("955", "956", "957", "960", "965"))
#> Warning in ensure_codes(residents, municipality, c("955", "956", "957", : Codes not in the code list: municipality
#> ℹ 1 row in 1 group:
#>     municipality  year
#>     <chr>        <int>
#>   1 95            2020

A new extract: describe_changes()

A register is delivered again and again, and the same person-year should not change between deliveries unless it was corrected. describe_changes() compares two extracts by their key:

before <- tibble(cpr = c("a", "b", "c"), year = 2023,
                 sex = c("F", "M", "F"), born = c(1950, 1960, NA))
after  <- tibble(cpr = c("a", "b", "d"), year = 2023,
                 sex = c("F", "F", "M"), born = c(1950, 1960, 1990))

describe_changes(before, after, cpr, year)
#> ── Changes by cpr, year ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 3 rows before, 3 rows now, 2 keys in both
#> 
#> • New keys: 1 (33.3%)
#> • Keys gone: 1 (33.3%)
#> • Keys with a changed value: 1 (50.0%)
#> 
#> Changes per column, among the keys in both:
#>     column changed went_missing filled_in share 
#>   1 sex          1            0         0 50.00%
#>   2 born         0            0         0 0.00%

Within a lifetime: ensure_within()

Registers are updated at different times, so a linked extract can hold a person after death or emigration, or income before birth. ensure_within() requires each row to lie between its own bounds, usually joined on from the population register. A yearly row counts by the year, so the year of death itself is fine:

panel <- tibble(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b"),
  year  = c(2022, 2023, 2024, 2022, 2023),
  born  = as.Date(c("1950-04-01", "1950-04-01", "1950-04-01", "2023-01-10", "2023-01-10")),
  death = as.Date(c("2023-05-01", "2023-05-01", "2023-05-01", NA, NA))
)

ensure_within(panel, year, from = born, to = death)
#> Warning in ensure_within(panel, year, from = born, to = death): Rows outside: year within born to death
#> ℹ 2 rows in 2 groups:
#>     outside      year born       death      cpr
#>     <chr>       <dbl> <date>     <date>     <chr>
#>   1 after death  2024 1950-04-01 2023-05-01 a
#>   2 before born  2022 2023-01-10 NA         b

From spells to a panel: spells_to_panel()

spells_to_panel() turns spells into one row per unit and year (or by = "quarter"/"month"), with the status at primo and ultimo. By default primo is the previous ultimo, so primo 2021 is the status on 31 December 2020.

In an education register the status is the outcome of the spell, passed or dropped out. With status_is = "outcome", a running spell shows as ongoing and the outcome applies from the end date until a new spell starts:

education <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "b"),
  start  = as.Date(c("2018-08-15", "2021-08-15", "2019-08-15")),
  end    = as.Date(c("2021-06-20", NA,           "2020-03-01")),
  status = c("passed", "in progress", "dropped out")
)

education |>
  spells_to_panel(cpr, start, end, status,
                  from = 2018, to = 2022,
                  status_is = "outcome", ongoing = "in progress")
#> # A tibble: 10 × 4
#>    cpr    year primo       ultimo     
#>    <chr> <int> <chr>       <chr>      
#>  1 a      2018 NA          in progress
#>  2 a      2019 in progress in progress
#>  3 a      2020 in progress in progress
#>  4 a      2021 in progress in progress
#>  5 a      2022 in progress in progress
#>  6 b      2018 NA          NA         
#>  7 b      2019 NA          in progress
#>  8 b      2020 in progress dropped out
#>  9 b      2021 dropped out dropped out
#> 10 b      2022 dropped out dropped out

With the default status_is = "state", the status holds for the whole spell (enrolled, on leave) and is NA outside spells. from and to give every unit the same window, which makes a balanced panel.

Status on a panel you have: add_spell_status()

Often the panel exists already, and the spells should only add a status to it. A left_join(join_by(between())) does that until the data gets messy: overlapping spells duplicate rows, and an ongoing spell with no end matches nothing. add_spell_status() keeps the rows of the panel exactly as they are and uses the rules of spells_to_panel():

population <- data.frame(cpr  = c("a", "a", "b", "c"),
                         year = c(2020, 2021, 2020, 2020))

population |>
  add_spell_status(education, cpr, year, start, end, status,
                   status_is = "outcome", ongoing = "in progress")
#>   cpr year status_primo status_ultimo
#> 1   a 2020  in progress   in progress
#> 2   a 2021  in progress   in progress
#> 3   b 2020  in progress   dropped out
#> 4   c 2020         <NA>          <NA>

Valid boundaries and reference coverage

Validate spell boundaries before checking their relationships. Missing ends represent ongoing spells; open_end = FALSE requires closed spells.

ensure_valid_spells(education, start, end)
#> ✔ Valid spells: start to end

Check that each observation can be linked to a reference register. Duplicate reference keys do not multiply rows, and missing keys do not match unless na_matches = "na" is specified.

observations <- tibble(cpr = c("a", "b", "c"), year = 2020)
reference <- tibble(person_id = c("a", "b"), year = 2020)
ensure_matched(observations, reference, by = c(cpr = "person_id", "year"))
#> Warning in ensure_matched(observations, reference, by = c(cpr = "person_id", : Keys missing from the reference: cpr, year
#> ℹ 1 row found:
#>     cpr    year
#>     <chr> <dbl>
#>   1 c      2020

Codes valid at the observation time

A temporal code list has code, valid_from and valid_to. Bounds are inclusive, missing bounds are open, and a code may have several intervals. Time and bounds use the same scale: dates, date-times, or numeric periods. Missing observation times fail for non-missing codes. na_ok controls missing codes separately.

codebook <- tibble(code = c("A", "B"),
                   valid_from = c(2015, 2020), valid_to = c(2019, NA_real_))
coded <- tibble(classification = c("A", "A", "B"), year = c(2019, 2020, 2020))
ensure_codes(coded, classification, codebook, time = year)
#> Warning in ensure_codes(coded, classification, codebook, time = year): Codes not in the code list: classification
#> ℹ 1 row in 1 group:
#>     classification  year
#>     <chr>          <dbl>
#>   1 A               2020

Personal data and large registers

inshape is made for interactive review of registers, at the console in the environment where the data lives. The offending rows of a check are personal data, so inshape writes nothing to disk, neither rows nor a log. A failure shows the count and the first rows. Wrap the check in violations() to get all of them, to look at in the session; when the check passes, it returns no rows:

gaps <- violations(ensure_balanced(panel, cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE))
#> ✔ No gaps in year per cpr
gaps
#> # A tibble: 0 × 4
#> # ℹ 4 variables: cpr <chr>, year <dbl>, born <date>, death <date>

A DuckDB or Arrow table is checked where it lives, and only the count and the first rows are fetched into R. See ?checkpoints for both.
